# f5xc_nat_policy (Data Source)

NAT Policy NAT Policy object represents the configuration of Network Address Translation parameters on F5XC Customer Edge sites. The following properties can be configured in this object: Site where the NAT objects are applicable Ingress points where the NAT policies need to be applied Match criteria of the packet to apply NAT Policy Action to take if the Match criteria passes

<a id="nestedatt--rules--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.action`

Read-Only:

- `source_nat_choice` (Attributes) NAT Choose between source NAT or Virtual Subnet NAT (Static NAT). When a match occurs, source NAT will change the original source address to either an SNAT Pool for East-West Scenarios or Cloud Elastic IP Object when traffic is destined to the internet. Virtual Subnet NAT is a static NAT implementation that changes the source & destination address and is mostly used for overlapping address scenarios. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--action--source_nat_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--rules--action--source_nat_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.action.source_nat_choice`

Read-Only:

- `dynamic` (Attributes) Source NAT Source NAT to either an SNAT Pool for East-West traffic or to a Cloud Elastic IP Object. Note that for a 3-node cluster the IPv4 prefix list should provide a minimum of 3 addresses to ensure each node gets an IP address from the pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--action--source_nat_choice--dynamic))
- `virtual_cidr` (String) Virtual Subnet NAT Virtual Subnet NAT is static NAT that does a one-to-one translation between the real source IP CIDR in the policy and the virtual CIDR in a bidirectional fashion. The range of the real CIDR and virtual CIDRs should be the same (e.g. if the real CIDR has the CIDR 10.10.10.0/24, the virtual CIDR has 100.100.100.0/24.
